compiled_rule.technosphere_information_loss: Exact ecoinvent3.9cutoff Quebec bark market reconstruction per signed kilogram measured as dry mass. Preserve all three producer shares separately: hardwood sawmill bark, softwood sawmill bark and allocated bark from soft fibreboard production using wet/dry processes. Use the corresponding complete native RER hardwood/softwood sawmill and soft-fibreboard bark co-product inventories, not full fibreboard output or an all-hardwood bark substitute. All source/native reference outputs are positive1kg measured as dry mass, factor+1. Source wet mass2.4kg per drykg does not justify a wet-mass multiplier. Native allocated inventories retain their own allocation, wood/energy/resource uptake and emission models; do not reallocate, add main-board burdens or an avoided-product credit. RER is a geographic screening proxy for Quebec. Species within the hardwood/softwood class, mill yields, allocation, wet/dry process mix, density/moisture, carbon, energy, infrastructure, vintage, native biosphere exclusions and internal uncertainty can differ, with unquantified score effects. Original final-product lorry tonne-km, signed quantities and supported uncertainty/formulas remain unchanged. Native precursor transport is inside production; original market final delivery is added once, using the complete RER fleet service with geographic/fleet/load/fuel/standard warnings and no extra diesel or empty-return multiplier. Separate caller emissions and carbon-resource exchanges remain unchanged. No source exchange is omitted, no carbon/energy/moisture correction is invented, and no main-product or co-product quantities are renormalized. Only independently inspected exact3.9cutoff Quebec bark qualifies. RoW pulp/paper bark, window-frame pellet co-products and residual-wood transformations remain unapproved; no other source version or consequential/reverse route is inferred. Full pulp heat and steel transformation/export remain unfinished.
